programs.name: ftnunstrip
programs.purpose: Wrap groups of binary floats in Fortran-style record markers.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: FTNUNSTRIP - convert C binary floats to Fortran style floats

params.name: n1
params.description: Number of floats per record; an incomplete final record is an error.

params.name: outpar
params.description: File receiving the record count as n=.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Record markers are native integers containing FSIZE*n1, and their byte order and integer representation are platform-dependent. Very large n1 can overflow the marker calculation.
programs.difficulty_reason: It buffers one fixed-size record and writes native record markers around its floats.

test_cases.command: suplane nt=16 ntr=2 | sustrip | ftnunstrip n1=1 outpar=/dev/stderr

test_cases.description: Wrap one trace's samples per record.
test_cases.command: suspike nt=16 ntr=2 | sustrip | ftnunstrip n1=16 outpar=/dev/stderr

programs.license_note: Credits say it is based on ftnstrip by Jack K. Cohen.

programs.name: h2b
programs.purpose: Convert pairs of hexadecimal digits to binary floats with each value subtracted from 255.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: H2B - convert 8 bit hexidecimal floats to binary

params.name: outpar
params.description: File receiving the total number of converted values.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: The parser advances exactly two characters after each sscanf call, including when whitespace or a short final field is present; malformed or oddly formatted lines can therefore be misread or access beyond the line terminator.
programs.difficulty_reason: It parses hexadecimal fields line by line and performs a simple per-value conversion.

test_cases.description: Convert hexadecimal bytes derived from a small trace.
test_cases.command: suspike nt=8 ntr=1 | sustrip | od -An -v -tx1 | tr -d ' \n' | h2b outpar=/dev/stderr

test_cases.description: Convert multiple short hexadecimal input lines.
test_cases.command: suplane nt=8 ntr=2 | sustrip | od -An -v -tx1 -w4 | tr -d ' ' | h2b outpar=/dev/stderr

programs.name: i2a
programs.purpose: Format native binary integers as rows of ASCII decimal integers.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: I2A - convert binary integers to ascii

params.name: n1
params.description: Number of integers per output line; an incomplete final line is an error.

params.name: outpar
params.description: File receiving the output line count as n=.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Input integers use the native C int size, representation, and byte order.
programs.difficulty_reason: It reads fixed-size groups of integers and prints each group.

test_cases.description: Print pairs of integers converted from generated float samples.
test_cases.command: suspike nt=16 ntr=2 | sustrip | recast in=float out=int outpar=/dev/stderr | i2a n1=2 outpar=/dev/stderr
suplane nt=16 ntr=2 | sustrip | recast in=float out=int outpar=/dev/stderr | i2a n1=8 outpar=/dev/stderr

programs.license_note: Credits identify Balazs Nemeth of Potash Corporation and say the program is based on b2a.c by Jack K. Cohen.

programs.name: ibm2float
programs.purpose: Convert headerless IBM-format floating-point words to native binary floats.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: IBM2FLOAT - convert IBM tape FLOATS to native binary FLOATS

params.name: endian
params.default: computed: 1 on a big-endian host, 0 on a little-endian host
params.description: Selects whether input words are byte-swapped before conversion; the HPUX implementation ignores it.

params.name: outpar
params.description: File receiving the number of converted values as n=.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Assumes 32-bit int and float and type-puns float storage through int pointers. Signed shifts in byte swapping can be undefined or implementation-dependent. In the regular implementation, a nonzero IBM word with zero mantissa warns but then loops forever; the HPUX implementation instead returns zero. Overflow saturates and underflow becomes zero.
programs.difficulty_reason: It converts one word at a time using bit masks and shifts.

test_cases.description: Round-trip generated floats through IBM format with detected host byte order.
test_cases.command: suspike nt=16 ntr=2 | sustrip | float2ibm outpar=/dev/stderr | ibm2float outpar=/dev/stderr

test_cases.description: Exercise explicitly selected little-endian handling on a little-endian host.
test_cases.command: suplane nt=16 ntr=2 | sustrip | float2ibm endian=0 outpar=/dev/stderr | ibm2float endian=0 outpar=/dev/stderr

programs.license_note: Credits say the program is based on code by Jack K. Cohen; the conversion routine credits Brian Sumner and notes modifications by Toralf Foerster and M. J. Rutty.

programs.name: recast
programs.purpose: Convert a stream of native binary numbers from one C data type to another.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: RECAST - RECAST data type (convert from one data type to another)

params.name: in
params.description: Input type: float, double, int, char, uchar, short, long, or ulong.

params.name: out
params.description: Output type; supported pairs are enumerated in the source, and equal or unsupported pairs error.

params.name: outpar
params.description: File receiving the number of converted values as n=; the selfdoc calls this n1.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Native type widths and byte order affect the stream. Float-to-integer paths convert through double and round halves away from zero; out-of-range floating-to-integer conversions have undefined behavior, and narrowing signed integer conversions can be implementation-defined. The int-to-long and int-to-ulong branches actually read long-sized input; char-to-ulong and uchar-to-ulong write signed long. The initial type check uses OR across input and output types, so some invalid types reach the unsupported-pair error.
programs.difficulty_reason: It selects a type pair and converts each input value independently.

test_cases.command: suplane nt=16 ntr=2 | sustrip | recast in=float out=double outpar=/dev/stderr
suspike nt=16 ntr=2 | sustrip | recast in=float out=int outpar=/dev/stderr
suspike nt=16 ntr=2 | sustrip | recast in=float out=int outpar=/dev/stderr | recast in=int out=short outpar=/dev/stderr

programs.name: swapbytes
programs.purpose: Swap the byte order of each value in a binary stream.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: SWAPBYTES - SWAP the BYTES of various  data types

params.name: in
params.description: Input type: float, double, short, ushort, long, ulong, or int.

params.name: outpar
params.description: File receiving the number of converted values as n=; the selfdoc calls this n1.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: The code assumes fixed widths for the swap functions, but reads and writes long and unsigned long using sizeof(long); on platforms with 8-byte longs, the 4-byte swap routines do not swap the complete value.
programs.difficulty_reason: It applies a byte-swap routine independently to each input value.

test_cases.command: suplane nt=16 ntr=2 | sustrip | swapbytes in=float outpar=/dev/stderr
suspike nt=16 ntr=2 | sustrip | recast in=float out=short outpar=/dev/stderr | swapbytes in=short outpar=/dev/stderr
suspike nt=16 ntr=2 | sustrip | recast in=float out=double outpar=/dev/stderr | swapbytes in=double outpar=/dev/stderr

programs.license_note: Credits say Jens Hartmann of Institut fur Geophysik, Hamburg supplied the byte-swapping subroutines.
